alt: New concrete patio around a green pool behind a house

problems: Image A also changes the pool. Weeds are growing inside the pool at the right end and along the coping, and the water level or waterline looks different from B. In B the right end is clear, with a yellowish stain on the pool floor.
Image A has a dark patch on the concrete near the covered patio, plus stains and tire-like marks on the slab. B doesn't have these, so they look invented.
The pool coping in A is broken, uneven and weedy. In B it is a clean, continuous edge, so the pool edge was changed along with the surface.
A small white pipe stub sticks out of the slab at the left in B. A doesn't have it, so an object is missing.
The cracked slab pattern in A is heavy and a bit exaggerated. It looks somewhat synthetic, but it is still plausible as a real photo.
The pool coping in A is a different material and shape from B. A has rough, irregular, stained stone coping, and B has clean, pale, uniform coping.
The pool water in A is greener and clearer, with the pool wall visible. B shows an orange or yellow stained area at the shallow end. This is a change beyond the concrete surface.

A has a sinkhole or hole, weeds and grass growing through cracks, and large cracks in the concrete. B shows none of these. This is the intended before-state of the surface, but the damage is heavy and looks somewhat staged.
A has a pale yellow stain and dark patches that look slightly painted on, not like natural wear.
A is missing the small white pipe stub visible at the left edge of the slab in B.
The house, stairs, railings, logs, retaining wall and trees all match. I saw no warping, smeared text or perspective errors.
